questions.prompt: A proposal for Metric calculation measures 251/s and reserves 28% for failure, recovery, or skew. It plans steady demand at 192.1/s and has no specific shed rule. Should it ship? Name the deciding number and reversal evidence.
questions.correct_answer: Decline Metric calculation at 192.1/s. The deciding number is 251 x 0.72 = 180.7/s, so planned demand exceeds the usable region by 11.4/s. Approve later if repeated measurements lift usable capacity above 192.1/s or a named policy removes at least 11.4/s of deferrable work before saturation.
questions.explanation: The decision turns on the usable capacity after the reserve, not the nominal measurement alone. The reversal condition is tied to metric calculation demand and the protection policy in this case.
questions.grading_notes: Full credit gives the stated decision, computes 180.7/s, compares it with planned demand, and names a scenario-specific reversal condition.
